## Keys

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `u` | Opens and closes the popover. |
| `]` | Moves the ladder setting one level up. |
| `[` | Moves the ladder setting one level down. |

: Default keys. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

You can change the keys with the `keys` option.
See the [Reference](reference.qmd#options).

Veil compares `event.key`, not `keyCode`.
Thus `[` and `]` work on keyboards where they need AltGr, such as AZERTY.
The keys have no effect in an `input`, a `textarea`, a `select`, or an editable element.

In Reveal.js, Veil adds entries to the `?` help.
It adds the entries for `keys.level-up` and `keys.level-down` only when the document has a ladder.
It adds the entry for `keys.menu` when that key is set.

### Key conflicts

A key can be the same as a key of Reveal.js or Quarto, or the same as another Veil key.
Then Veil writes a warning, and the runtime does not bind this key.
The keys that Veil checks are:

- Reveal.js: `n`, Space, `p`, PageUp, PageDown, the arrows, `h`, `j`, `k`, `l`, Home, End, `b`, `v`, `.`, `;`, `:`, `/`, `f`, `a`, `g`, `?`, F1, Esc, and `o`.
- Quarto decks: `s`, `m`, `e`, and `r`.
- Quarto website search, in HTML: `f`, `/`, and `s`.
- Chalkboard, when it is enabled: `c`, `b`, Delete, `-`, Backspace, `x`, `y`, and `d`.

## Popover

The popover has the controls for all the groups.

- The ladder is a segmented control with one segment for `0` and one for each declared level.
  A segment for a level with more than one group shows the labels with `+`, for example `Advanced + Notes`.
- Below the ladder, there is one `role="switch"` control for each independent group.
- While the popover is open, it stops key events, so Space and Esc do not go to Reveal.js.
- Esc closes the popover.
  The focus goes back to the element that had the focus before the popover opened, else to the document body.

In Reveal.js, the Tools menu has one entry, "Veil…", that opens the popover.

## Floating button

The button is an eye icon.
It opens the popover.

- `button.enabled: auto` shows the button in `html` and not in `revealjs`.
- `button.position` sets the corner: `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, or `bottom-right`.
  The default, `bottom-left`, does not cover the Quarto back-to-top button.
- In Reveal.js, the button is outside `.slides`, so it does not scale with the slides.
- The button and the popover are hidden in Reveal.js print mode and in `@media print`.

## Toast

The toast is a short message that shows after each change of state.
It shows after a change from a key, the popover, the Tools menu, or the API.
It does not show at load time.

- For an independent group, the text is `Backup · hidden`.
- For a ladder change, the text is `Level 2 · Advanced, Expert`, or `Level 0 · none`.
- It is a small pill at the bottom centre of the screen.
  It shows for about 1.5 seconds, then fades out.
- A new toast replaces the current toast.
- It has `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"`.
  With `prefers-reduced-motion`, it does not fade.

The option `toast` sets where it shows:

| Value | Where the toast shows |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | In the speaker view while it is open, else in the main window. |
| `main` | In the main window. |
| `speaker` | In the speaker view only. |
| `false` | Nowhere. |

: Values of the option `toast`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

In HTML, `auto` and `speaker` are the same as `main`.

## Theme

Set these CSS custom properties to change the colours and the corner radius.

- `--veil-bg`
- `--veil-fg`
- `--veil-accent`
- `--veil-radius`

The default values come from the Bootstrap variables in HTML and from the Reveal.js theme variables in Reveal.js.
